name: Neu-Laxova Syndrome due to 3-Phosphoserine Phosphatase Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of severe congenital microcephaly with brain malformations
Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including proptosis, micrognathia, and cleft lip/palate
Congenital arthrogryposis multiplex with limb contractures
Biallelic pathogenic variants in the PSPH gene encoding 3-phosphoserine phosphatase
Severe intrauterine growth restriction documented prenatally or at birth

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major clinical features plus genetic confirmation of biallelic PSPH mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally or at birth due to severe phenotype and confirmed by molecular genetic testing.

severe small head and brain smoothness

unusual facial shape with eye protrusion

congenital stiff joints and limb deformities
baby smaller than expected in womb
split lip and/or roof of mouth

poor lung growth causing breathing problems

imaging: Brain MRI showing lissencephaly and severe microcephaly
Prenatal ultrasound revealing intrauterine growth restriction and limb contractures
other: Characteristic facial dysmorphism and arthrogryposis on clinical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Caused by mutations in PSAT1 gene
Similar phenotype but may have milder skin involvement
Includes Neu-Laxova syndrome and other serine biosynthesis defects
May lack severe microcephaly and arthrogryposis

redFlags: Severe congenital microcephaly with brain malformations
Characteristic facial dysmorphism with proptosis and cleft lip/palate
